findings.evidence: grep `IsSepClosed` in FormalGroup/: hits only at Height.lean:11, 374 and 388. Mathlib/FieldTheory/IsSepClosed.lean:8 is `public import Mathlib.FieldTheory.Galois.Basic`. The three files above import TauCeti.RingTheory.FormalGroup.Height.
findings.fix: Move the theorem and the import to a new file for the separably-closed classification. If it sits beside Height, do `git mv Height.lean Height/Basic.lean` and add `Height/SepClosed.lean`; do not create a flat `HeightSepClosed.lean`. Update the three importers' imports to match.
findings.issue: `FormalGroup.exists_coeff_nsmulSeries_homothety_smul_eq_one` is the only use of `IsSepClosed`, but it forces `public import Mathlib.FieldTheory.IsSepClosed` (line 11) into the base height file. That import brings in Galois theory and reaches `Rigidity.lean`, `Logarithm/InfiniteHeight.lean` and `Frobenius/Factorization.lean`, none of which use separable closure.

findings.evidence: NSMul/Basic.lean:349 `theorem subst_nsmulSeries (f : FormalGroupHom F G) (n : ℕ)` inside `namespace TauCeti.FormalGroupHom` (lines 343–361). The new lemma's proof uses only that result plus `PowerSeries.coeff_subst_eq_mul` and `PowerSeries.coeff_subst_eq_mul_pow`.
findings.fix: Move it to `TauCeti/RingTheory/FormalGroup/NSMul/Basic.lean` in `namespace TauCeti.FormalGroupHom`, right after `subst_nsmulSeries` (line 349). If needed, add a private import of `TauCeti.RingTheory.PowerSeries.Substitution` there.
findings.issue: `TauCeti.FormalGroupHom.coeff_nsmulSeries_mul_coeff_one_pow_of_le_order` holds over any `CommRing` and any `n`. It does not mention height and depends only on `FormalGroupHom.subst_nsmulSeries` and the new substitution lemmas, so Height.lean is the wrong home.

summary: The separably-closed normalization theorem adds a Galois-theory import (`Mathlib.FieldTheory.IsSepClosed`) to the base `Height.lean` and every file that imports it, and a general ring-level lemma about `nsmulSeries` sits in Height.lean instead of next to `FormalGroupHom.subst_nsmulSeries`.
